description:
You are a senior hydrologist at the Indiana Department of Natural Resources tasked with calibrating the HEC-RAS White River flood model to match a recorded peak stage from a recent storm event. A terminal is open in the Muncie HEC-RAS project directory.

A calibration target file has been placed at ~/Documents/observed_gauge_data.txt. This file contains the peak water surface elevation recorded at the USGS gauge during the storm event that the model should reproduce.

The HEC-RAS Muncie project's main channel Manning's roughness coefficient (n) has been set to an incorrect value and must be adjusted. Manning's n is stored in the 2D geometry data within the template HDF5 file (Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf) under the dataset path: Geometry/2D Flow Areas/Muncie/Manning's n. You can read and modify HDF5 datasets directly using Python with h5py.

The main channel cells (those near the river thalweg) have lower elevation values in the terrain. In the Manning's n dataset, the main channel cells can be identified as those whose corresponding terrain elevation (in Geometry/2D Flow Areas/Muncie/Cells Minimum Elevation) is below the floodplain (use a threshold to separate the two zones; the bimodal distribution of cell elevations will show the channel vs. floodplain separation).

Your calibration tasks:
1. Read the observed peak stage target from ~/Documents/observed_gauge_data.txt.
2. Conduct a systematic Manning's n sensitivity study: run at least 3 simulations with different main-channel Manning's n values. For each run, modify the n values in the HDF5, run RasUnsteady, extract the overall peak WSE from Muncie.p04.hdf, and record the results.
3. Log all calibration runs to ~/Documents/hec_ras_results/calibration_log.csv with columns: run_id,mannings_n,simulated_peak_wse_ft,residual_ft (residual = simulated - observed, positive means model over-predicts).
4. Select the n value that produces the simulated peak WSE closest to the observed target. Apply that n value to Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf as the final calibrated model.
5. Write ~/Documents/hec_ras_results/calibration_report.txt documenting: the observed peak stage, the calibrated Manning's n value, the final simulated peak WSE, and the calibration residual.

Note: The RasUnsteady executable reads from Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf and writes results to Muncie.p04.hdf. You must modify Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf (the template) before each run. Run command: RasUnsteady Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf x04
